name: Sennacherib
role: King of Assyria who besieged Jerusalem
whenBasis: From the Assyrian king lists and eponym chronicles; his campaign against Judah is dated 701 BC.
summary: King of Assyria who in Hezekiah's fourteenth year came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them. He sent his officials with an army to demand Jerusalem's surrender and a letter mocking the LORD. That night the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp; Sennacherib returned to Nineveh, where two of his sons killed him as he worshipped in the temple of Nisroch.
body: He besieges Lachish, receives Hezekiah's tribute of silver and gold, and still sends the Rabshakeh to Jerusalem. His letter lists the gods of the nations that could not save their lands. Isaiah's oracle answers him: the virgin daughter of Zion despises him, and he will return by the way he came.

later.text: His palace at Nineveh was lined with reliefs of the siege and capture of Lachish, now in the British Museum.

sources.title: Lachish reliefs, British Museum 124904–124915
sources.note: from the South-West Palace, Nineveh, excavated by Austen Henry Layard

later.text: The Babylonian Chronicle records that he was killed by his son in a rebellion, in 681 BC.

media.caption: Sennacherib's army is destroyed (2 Kings 19:35), Gustave Doré, 1866.
